artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $E$ be a Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$. For each $n\in\mathbb N$, write $E^n$ for the $n$-fold Cartesian product. A multi-norm on $\{E^n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is a sequence $(\|\cdot\|_n)$ of norms, with $\|\cdot\|_1=\|\cdot\|$ on $E$, satisfying the four axioms: (A1) $\|(x_{\sigma(1)},\dots,x_{\sigma(n)})\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n$ for every permutation $\sigma$; (A2) $\|(\alpha_1 x_1,\dots,\alpha_n x_n)\|_n\le(\max_i|\alpha_i|)\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n$; (A3) $\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},0)\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1})\|_{n-1}$; (A4) $\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},x_{n-1})\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1})\|_{n-1}$.

For $1\le p\le q<\infty$, the $(p,q)$-multi-norm on $E$ is defined by
$$\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n^{(p,q)}=\sup\Big\{\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n |\langle x_i,\lambda_i\rangle|^q\Big)^{1/q}:\ \lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n\in E^*,\ \sup_{\|x\|\le1}\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|\langle x,\lambda_i\rangle|^p\Big)^{1/p}\le1\Big\}.$$

Two multi-norms $(\|\cdot\|_n^{[1]})$ and $(\|\cdot\|_n^{[2]})$ on $E$ are equivalent if there are constants $c,C>0$ with $c\|\cdot\|_n^{[1]}\le\|\cdot\|_n^{[2]}\le C\|\cdot\|_n^{[1]}$ for all $n$.

Problem. Fix $r$ with $1<r<2$ and take $E=\ell^r$. Determine, for all pairs $(p_1,q_1)$ and $(p_2,q_2)$ with $1\le p_i\le q_i<\infty$, exactly when the $(p_1,q_1)$-multi-norm based on $\ell^r$ is equivalent to the $(p_2,q_2)$-multi-norm based on $\ell^r$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of equivalences of $(p,q)$-multi-norms based on $\ell^r$ is complete for $r=1$ and for $r\ge 2$, but only partial results are known in the range $1<r<2$, where the question is connected to estimates for absolutely $(q,p)$-summing norms. No source found indicates a complete resolution in the intermediate range.

status_evidence.title: Equivalences involving (p,q)-multi-norms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when (p,q)-multi-norms on L^r are equivalent; complete in some ranges of r, partial otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence problem for (p,q)-multi-norms on ℓ^r/L^r is fully resolved only for certain r, with gaps for 1<r<2.

status_evidence.title: Equivalence of multi-norms (arXiv:1304.2096)
status_evidence.snippet: Dales–Polyakov style memoir defining equivalence of multi-norms.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of equivalence of multi-norms was set up here; subsequent works addressed the (p,q) classification.
